answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent's identity to a staking collateral that is forfeited through slashing penalties whenever a duplicate proof appears. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay function enforces a network pulse that makes any cloning attempt incur negative expected attack utility. The resulting protocol achieves a robust Nash equilibrium, rendering identity forgery as improbable as a comet on a voyage. Recursive aggregation yields logarithmic proof size, enabling constant-time verification across the validator set.
